title: products.yaml — how a ticket becomes code, an environment and a verdict
description: The registry that makes one loop serve every application. A ticket resolves to repos, a branch, a stack profile and test commands from here alone, with no human looking anything up.

match.description: How a ticket resolves to this product. At least one criterion must be present, or every ticket matches everything.

customers.description: Names of the customer whose estate this product is. Outranks every other criterion: a ticket that says SaskTel is about SaskTel's estate whatever product vocabulary it also mentions. Two runs resolved to the wrong repository before this existed - one to infra because the ticket's Environment block names Keycloak, one to crm because "CRM" appeared once in an analysis sentence - while both named the customer in their title. List every spelling that appears on real tickets, including accented forms: "myLüm" never matched a "LUM" term.

repos.description: owner/name. Every repo listed is cloned by the registry check and must carry the plugin, AGENTS.md and REVIEW.md.

modules.description: For a container repo whose real content is sibling repos: directory under the parent checkout -> owner/name of the repo that fills it. Cloning the parent alone does NOT produce these; they are git-ignored by it. Unlike `repos` these are not clone-checked and are not expected to carry the plugin, AGENTS.md or REVIEW.md - they are libraries, not products. Clone only the ones a ticket needs.

multi_repo.description: When true, plan.md must produce per-repo tasks and a merge order, and nothing merges until every PR in the set is approved.

version_source.description: Where the resolved version comes from for a bug (e.g. a Jira field or a customer profile key). Absent means the branch policy alone decides.

forward_port.description: When a bug was fixed on a release branch, cherry-pick onto this branch as a draft PR. Conflicts escalate rather than silently skip.

topology_default.description: e.g. 2node. Per-process state is not a correctness mechanism above 1node.

liquibase.description: Whether the stack supports tag/rollbackToTag between attempts.

build.description: Build command. Absent means the product needs no build step before tests.

toolchain.description: Environment the build actually needs (JAVA_HOME, NODE_VERSION, ...), set for every agent on this product. Run 9a6ea7d0 read 6,820 'AspectJ source level is 1.5' errors from the wrong JDK as a defect in the repository, concluded nothing here could build, and opened three pull requests anyway.

atdd.description: Must emit xunit. The build loop parses a verdict, it does not grep logs.

regression.description: Named suite for the product's full regression.

ui_trace.description: Absent means UI evidence is legitimately n/a for this product.

compose_test.description: Infra oracle: a check that fails on current state and is idempotent when applied twice.

integration.description: Cross-module or cross-service tests. Must emit a machine-readable report named by `reports.integration`; a suite whose only output is a log cannot produce a per-scenario verdict.

security.description: Dependency, secret and static security checks. Required in practice for any product on an authorization, payment or personal-data path - SECURITY_GATE has nothing to read without it.

visual.description: Visual regression run. Playwright's own screenshot comparison; see agents/visual-qa.md for why no hosted vendor is used.

owners.description: Owner group per blast-radius label. money and protocol must be named for any product that has such paths.

suite.description: The product suite this belongs to (e.g. bss, aaa, core). Groups products that share infrastructure stacks and recipes; informational for routing, required for none.

reports.description: Where each test class writes its MACHINE-READABLE report, and in what format. A command without one of these can only ever yield a whole-suite pass/fail, which is why acceptance rows cannot be scored per row. A product with no `reports` entry for a class is not spec-capable for that class - a registry fact, not a per-run discovery.

glob.description: Path glob, relative to the repo root, matching the report file(s) this class writes.

format.description: How to parse it into per-case results. The trusted-root parser must read <testcase> elements, not only <testsuite> totals.
